text: Erkki Oja, born on 22 March 1948, is a Finnish computer scientist and Aalto Distinguished Professor in the Department of Information and Computer Science at Aalto University School of Science. He is known for developing Oja's rule, a model that describes how neurons in the brain or in artificial neural networks learn over time. Oja was born in Helsinki and studied at Helsinki University of Technology, where he earned his diploma engineer in 1972, licentiate in technology in 1975, and Doctor of Technology in 1977. From 1976 to 1981, he served as a research fellow at the Academy of Finland, and from 1977 to 1978, he was a research associate at the Center for Cognitive Science at Brown University. Since 1981, he held a professorship in applied mathematics at Kuopio University (now University of Eastern Finland). From 1983 to 1984, he was a visiting research scholar at Tokyo Institute of Technology. From 1987 to 1993, he was a professor in computer science at the Lappeenranta University of Technology. He returned to the Helsinki University of Technology (now Aalto University) in 1993 as a professor in computer science and retired in 2015. Oja is a Fellow of the International Association for Pattern Recognition and the IEEE, and a member of the Finnish Academy of Sciences. He served as chairman of the European Neural Network Society from 2000 to 2005 and as chairman of the Academy of Finland’s Research Council for Natural Sciences and Engineering from 2007 to 2012. In 2019, he was awarded the Frank Rosenblatt Award for his contributions to artificial intelligence research. Oja was a member of the Board of Governors for the International Neural Network Society (INNIS) in 2003 and received honorary doctorates from Uppsala University and Lappeenranta University of Technology in 2008.
